lesson.title: Project clinic: reproducible artifacts and defensible conclusions
lesson.short: Environment · data lineage · smoke tests · report assembly
lesson.timeMeaning: Suggested independent study minutes; not scheduled contact time
lesson.lead: A useful artifact lets another person trace a figure back to inputs, code, settings and raw measurements.
goals: Package the evidence required to rerun a result.
Separate a smoke test from a full scientific reproduction.
Audit cost, data permission, limitations and claims before presenting.

sections.title: Start here: prerequisites and course status
sections.html:
Study path. Bring one raw result and its configuration. Trace how it becomes a figure before assembling the full artifact.

This original companion follows the supplied syllabus; it is not an Edinburgh lecture or verified Canvas assignment. Activities and timings are practice guidance. Assigned readings, assessment rules, deadlines and submission arrangements remain unverified.

sections.title: Define the artifact boundary
sections.html:
An artifact can contain source code, environment specification, data-access instructions, preprocessing scripts, configurations, raw results and plotting code. It should explain which result each command is intended to produce.

Pin code revisions and relevant dependency versions. Record CPU, GPU model and memory, driver/runtime, interconnect, RAM/storage, operating system and concurrency settings. A container helps preserve software but does not make hardware, datasets, external APIs or numerical behavior identical.

Describe dataset provenance, version, license and any permitted redistribution. If data cannot be shared, provide a synthetic smoke-test case and disclose which full results remain inaccessible. Do not redistribute restricted course files, private documents or credentials merely to make a package “complete”.

Primary sources: ACM SIGSIM PADS 2024: Reproducibility and Artifact Evaluation.

Key takeaway

Reproducibility is a traceable chain of evidence, not just a link to code.

sections.title: Worked example: a minimal run manifest
sections.html:
Original suggested manifest fields.

  • Identity: experiment ID, code commit, configuration hash, timestamp and responsible group member.
  • Inputs: dataset version/hash, query split IDs, model/embedding/prompt revision and random seed.
  • Environment: package lock, OS/runtime, hardware inventory, resource limits and background-load notes.
  • Protocol: warm-up, repetitions, trial order, timing boundary, timeout threshold and quality target.
  • Outputs: raw-result paths, error logs, correctness checks, generated figure and command.
  • Cost: elapsed device/CPU time, external-service calls, measured peak memory and any assumed price model.

Use checksums to detect changed files, not as evidence that data are correct. Keep secrets in approved environment/credential mechanisms and never commit tokens or keys. Logs can contain sensitive queries or document text, so inspect them before sharing.

Exercise: the README says “run latest version on the standard dataset.” What is missing?

Worked answer. Exact code/dependency versions, dataset identity and preprocessing, the command/configuration, hardware assumptions, expected output and acceptable variation. “Latest” and “standard” drift over time.

sections.title: A two-level execution path
sections.html:
Smoke test: run a tiny public/synthetic input that checks installation, schema, result correctness and output paths. It should complete quickly enough to diagnose setup. State that it does not reproduce the paper-scale performance result.

Full run: list realistic resource/time requirements, dataset preparation, the evaluation command, raw output format and figure-generation command. Include a resume/retry policy and warnings about expensive API calls or disk usage. Do not silently launch a paid cloud job from a setup script.

Ask a group member to follow the instructions from a clean allowed environment. Record discrepancies: changed defaults, unavailable packages, missing paths or nondeterminism. If the clean rerun differs, investigate rather than copying the old chart into the new report.

Exercise: the smoke test matches expected output. Can you claim the benchmark is reproduced?

Worked answer. No. It validates the basic execution path on a tiny input. Performance reproduction requires the declared dataset, protocol, environment and comparison, with reported differences and uncertainty.

sections.title: Budget the experiment rather than only the final run
sections.html:
Original planning example. Suppose each query repetition uses one GPU for 6 minutes. For 20 configurations and 5 repetitions each, query work is 20×5×6=600 GPU-minutes, or 10 GPU-hours. Count setup separately:

CostDeclared resource and reuse ruleTotal
Data preparation1 CPU-hour once for the shared dataset1 CPU-hour
Index build, reused4 GPU-minutes once per configuration20×4=80 GPU-minutes
Index build, rebuiltAlternative: 4 GPU-minutes per repetition20×5×4=400 GPU-minutes

With reused GPU builds, GPU work is 600+80=680 GPU-minutes (11⅓ GPU-hours); with a rebuild every repetition it is 1,000 GPU-minutes (16⅔ GPU-hours). The CPU-hour is a different resource and must not be added as a GPU-hour. If builds use CPU instead, label their time accordingly. GPU-hours also need not equal elapsed wall time when work overlaps or uses multiple devices. Builds remain outside the timed query region but inside the experiment budget. Stopping after the first successful run cannot answer a variability question.

For a one- or two-H100 project, check memory headroom before increasing dataset size and save intermediate results. A smaller complete matrix can be more informative than one oversized run that consumes the whole budget. Keep exploratory and final runs separate.

A clear stopping condition is evidence-based: the planned matrix is complete, a feasibility assumption fails, the bounded budget is reached, or additional work requires approval. Report which condition ended the study.

sections.title: Assemble a report that does not overclaim
sections.html:
A practical structure is: question; motivation and related work; design; assumptions; methodology; results; ablations; limitations; conclusion; artifact instructions. Put the central claim beside the plot that supports it and make axis units, sample count and quality target visible.

Maintain a claim-evidence checklist. For each sentence such as “scales better”, name the scaling axis, held-constant resources, workload, uncertainty and figure. Separate measured results, theoretical results, estimates and future work. Fabricated “representative” data must never be presented as an experiment.

Before the symposium, check that every group member can explain the main result and one failure case. Use the instructor’s confirmed deliverable and submission instructions when assembling this report.

Exercise: you estimated memory from vector dimensions but never measured peak allocation. How should it appear?

Worked answer. Label it an analytical estimate, list omitted buffers/workspace, and avoid calling it measured peak memory. If capacity feasibility is central to the claim, instrument the actual run or disclose that the claim remains untested.

Key takeaway

State what ran, what was measured and what remains an inference.

questions.question: Does a container alone guarantee bit-identical scientific reproduction?
options: No; hardware, data, external services and numerical/runtime behavior also matter.
Yes, regardless of hardware or input data.
Yes, if the image is large enough.
No, so containers have no value.
questions.explanation: Containers preserve part of the software environment. Reproducibility still depends on the complete evidence and execution boundary.

options: The paper-scale performance result is reproduced.
The basic execution path works on that test input.
Every dataset license permits redistribution.
The main hypothesis is universally true.
questions.explanation: A smoke test checks setup and a small functional path, not the full scientific claim.

120 GPU-minutes

questions.question: What should happen to API keys before sharing an artifact?
options: Remove them from code/logs and document approved credential setup without exposing secrets.
Put them in the figure caption.
Encode them in base64.
Include them so reviewers can run immediately.
questions.explanation: Encoding is not protection. Shared artifacts and logs must not expose credentials or unauthorized data.
